usage: gnd synth [-h] [--out OUT]
                 [--class {conforming,boundary,violating,all}] [--pool POOL]
                 [--seed SEED] [--baseline-seed BASELINE_SEED] [--seeds SEEDS]
                 [--format {text,json}]
                 model

Generate labelled synthetic populations, each with a provenance SIDECAR.
--class conforming builds populations the checker accepts; --class violating
mutates a conforming baseline, one population per (constraint, operator) pair,
each admitted only after the real checker confirms the model-derived typed
prediction (D-05'); --class all does both. The development lane is
probabilistic by default: --seed omitted draws OS entropy per population and
records it, so data is fresh yet regenerable; --seed N is the deterministic
variant-regeneration path. --pool consumes an admitted pool artifact; an
omitted --pool builds and materialises a Faker pool beside the corpus. Exits 5
on a generator invariant failure, 6 on a quarantined checker/witness or
prediction/observation disagreement (C1).

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out OUT             output root for populations (default: .gnd/synth)
  --class {conforming,boundary,violating,all}
                        the population class to generate: conforming,
                        boundary, violating, or all. `boundary` derives cases
                        from the constraints' own declared bounds (D-06) and
                        includes the `no-subjects` and `unchecked` frontier
                        kinds
  --pool POOL           path to an admitted pool artifact (default: build a
                        Faker pool)
  --seed SEED           RNG seed (omitted: draw OS entropy, the probabilistic
                        development default)
  --baseline-seed BASELINE_SEED
                        seed of the conforming baseline a violating run
                        mutates (recorded in every violating sidecar so each
                        case is traceable to what it mutated; default: --seed,
                        else OS entropy)
  --seeds SEEDS         number of independent seed variants to generate for
                        every requested class (default 1, the lightweight dev
                        lane). --seeds 30 is the publication/degeneracy
                        invocation: 30 clean seeds give 95% confidence (rule
                        of three) that fewer than 10% of the GENERATOR's runs
                        are degenerate
  --format {text,json}  output rendering: human-readable text (default) or one
                        JSON payload

content.text:
The catalogue is now ordinary facts, and the model validates (exit 0, both layers checked). That got `codegen` working but not `synth`: I was wrong last time to say this change would unblock both.

- **`gnd codegen` works.** A trial run in the scratchpad generated the full project without errors.
- **`gnd synth` still refuses the model,** because it won't generate data for the two derived relations: the prerequisite chain and the per-term credit total. It's a deliberate refusal in `synth`, not a model error. Removing those two relations would make `synth` work, but then the chain-of-prerequisites rule and the 18-credit rule could no longer be checked, so I've left them in.

**What the change means in practice:**
- A population you check now has to include the catalogue facts itself, unless it doesn't touch them. Before, they came from the bound file automatically.
- Nothing stops a checked population from altering the catalogue. That's the tradeoff you accepted.
- `references/catalog.pop.json` is still there, as a plain population holding the spring catalogue that you can merge into test data.
- Earlier I ran the same Maya checks against a copy of the model with the catalogue as ordinary facts, and the planted violations were caught there too.

The change is recorded in the model's notes and in `model.verbalization.txt`.
